Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.

# Summary of Political Manifesto

This document presents a political programme focused on comprehensive reform across multiple policy areas, with detailed costings and implementation timelines.

## Core Economic Proposals

The manifesto proposes significant tax restructuring, including raising the income tax threshold to £20,000 annually (removing approximately 7 million people from income tax), reducing corporation tax rates progressively from 25% to 15%, and abolishing inheritance tax for estates under £2 million. Stamp duty reductions are proposed for properties under £750,000. Business measures include raising VAT thresholds to £150,000 and abolishing business rates for high street small and medium enterprises, offset by an online delivery tax on large multinational corporations.

## Immigration Policy

The document advocates for substantial immigration restrictions, including freezing non-essential immigration, implementing an employer immigration tax of 20% on foreign workers (with healthcare exemptions), barring student dependents from entering, and requiring five years' residency before benefit eligibility. Proposals include offshore processing of asylum seekers and immediate deportation of foreign nationals following criminal convictions.

## Healthcare Reform

Healthcare proposals maintain free services at point of delivery whilst introducing significant structural changes: tax exemptions for frontline NHS staff, 20% tax relief on private healthcare, and a voucher system allowing patients to access private treatment when NHS waiting times exceed specified thresholds. The manifesto supports increased use of independent healthcare capacity and calls for a public inquiry into excess deaths and vaccine-related harms.

## Energy and Environment

The document proposes abandoning net-zero emissions targets, scrapping renewable energy subsidies, and expanding North Sea oil and gas extraction alongside shale gas exploration. It advocates for nuclear energy development through small modular reactors whilst eliminating environmental levies on energy bills, claiming household savings of £500 annually.

## Justice and Policing

Proposals include recruiting 40,000 additional police officers, implementing mandatory life sentences for repeat violent offenders, building 10,000 new detention places, and adopting zero-tolerance policing approaches. The manifesto calls for expanding stop-and-search powers and reopening local magistrates' courts.

## Education

Educational reforms include curriculum changes emphasising national heritage, banning gender identity teaching in schools, providing 20% tax relief on independent school fees, and scrapping interest on student loans whilst restricting undergraduate numbers. Universities would be required to offer two-year degree options.

## Defence

Military spending would increase to 3% of GDP within six years, with pay reviews for armed forces personnel, a dedicated veterans ministry, and emphasis on domestic defence manufacturing. The document opposes integration with European defence structures.

## Housing and Infrastructure

Housing proposals include planning reform to fast-track brownfield development, prioritising local residents for social housing, and scrapping proposed rental reforms. The high-speed rail project would be cancelled, with funds redirected to regional transport improvements. A new ownership model for utilities would establish 50% public ownership alongside pension fund investment.

## Constitutional Changes

Proposed constitutional reforms include withdrawal from the European Convention on Human Rights, House of Lords reform, electoral system changes including consideration of proportional representation, and postal voting restrictions. The document advocates for replacing existing equality legislation and reforming public broadcasting funding.

## Financial Summary

The manifesto claims total potential savings of £150 billion annually through reduced government spending, benefit reforms, and eliminating net-zero costs, plus £10 billion from projected economic growth. Total costs are estimated at £141 billion annually, covering tax reductions, healthcare, defence, and other spending increases.
